newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Gaddum sees leeway on EMU deficit rule.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Gaddum sees leeway on EMU deficit rule.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann-Wilhelm Gaddum said on Friday he saw a certain leeway on the budget deficit criteria countries must meet to participate in the planned euro launch in 1999.

The Maastricht Treaty calls on countries to hold their budget deficits at no more than three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) but the Bundesbank on Thursday already stressed that sustainability of budgetary positions was as important as hitting the targets on the button.

"If a country has 2.9 percent (deficit ratio) and thus formally meets the criterion in 1997, and it is clear that this deficit will rise in the coming years to 3.6, 3.8 or four percent, that is a worse performance that a state which now has 3.3 percent but where it is clear it will have 3.1 percent the day after tomorrow," Gaddum told German radio.
